## Problem 1

I created a function that draws a birthday for each of `n_room` people, assuming 365 equally likely days, checks for duplicates and returns `TRUE` if at least two people share a birthday and `FALSE` if not. This function was created in a separate R script and saved under `source/birthday_repeated.R`. 

Function

```{r}
birthday_repeated
```


Run the function 10000 times for each group size between 2 and 50

```{r}
birthday_results_df = 
  expand_grid(
    n_people = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    repeated = map_lgl(n_people, birthday_repeated)
  )
```

Compute and plot probability of a shared birthday by group size 

```{r}
birthday_results_df |> 
  group_by(n_people) |> 
  summarize(prob_of_repeat = mean(repeated)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = n_people, y = prob_of_repeat)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Probability at least 2 people share a birthday by group size", 
    x = "Number of people",
    y = "Probability of a shared birthday"
  )
```

The probability that at least two people share a birthday increases as the group size increases. Interestingly, only about 23 people are needed for there to be a 50% chance that two people share a birthday, and with only 50 people, the chance increases to about 97%!
